dwelling_habits.dwelling: Higher intertidal mudflats behind red mangroves.
dwelling_habits.feeding: Makes energy from sunlight (and sometimes from clear shallow water light).
dwelling_habits.mating: Spreads by spores, seeds, propagules, or creeping rhizomes depending on the species.
dwelling_habits.socializing: Forms habitat structure that shelters fish, crabs, and invertebrates.

fun_facts: Leaves can excrete salt crystals you can taste.
Pneumatophores are the mangrove’s snorkels at low tide.

dwelling_habits.dwelling: Shallow reefs and rubble where algae grows thick.
dwelling_habits.food: Algae and coral rock scraped with fused teeth.
dwelling_habits.feeding: Loud crunching you can sometimes hear underwater.
dwelling_habits.mating: Aggregates to spawn; colors flash during courtship.
dwelling_habits.socializing: Often in loose schools sweeping a reef face.

fun_facts: Big blues look painted with one giant watercolor wash.
Their beak is many teeth fused into a chisel.

dwelling_habits.dwelling: Caribbean coral reefs and rocky shallows where algae coats the rock.
dwelling_habits.food: Turf algae and film scraped from reef surfaces.
dwelling_habits.feeding: Pecks and scrapes with a small beak-like mouth — a living reef janitor.
dwelling_habits.mating: Spawns in groups over the reef at dusk; eggs drift with the current.
dwelling_habits.socializing: Juveniles are bright yellow loners; adults may school or keep a cleaning circuit.

fun_facts: Kids know this look from cartoon reefs — the real fish prefers salad to adventure.
Those scalpels at the tail base are real: don’t grab a tang.
